text:
The rain lashed against the precinct windows, mirroring the storm raging inside Detective Howard’s chest. He stared at the file on his desk, the evidence damning and undeniable. It wasn't just a mistake; it was a pattern of corruption that stretched back years, implicating his partner, Jack.

Howard’s hand trembled as he reached for his coffee, the warmth doing little to thaw the ice in his veins. Jack, who had pulled him out of a burning building. Jack, who had been his best man. The loyalty they shared was supposed to be unshakable, a bond forged in decades of shared danger and silence. But now, that silence felt like complicity.

He thought about the retirement party planned for tomorrow. The cake, the speeches, the handshakes. If he turned this in, he would be the one to destroy it all. He would be the one to send Jack to prison. But if he didn’t, he would be betraying the badge he had worn for thirty years, and the victims who had been failed by Jack’s greed.

The phone rang, shattering the heavy quiet. It was Jack. "Hey, partner," Jack’s voice was warm, familiar, laced with the easy camaraderie of a lifetime. "Just wanted to say I’m proud of you. Tomorrow’s going to be a big day."

Howard gripped the phone tighter, his knuckles white. "Yeah," he managed, his voice rough. "Big day."

He looked back at the evidence. The conflict wasn't just about duty versus friendship; it was about who he was when no one was watching. Was he a detective, or was he just a man who had lost his way? The weight of the decision pressed down on him, heavier than any badge, heavier than any gun. He had to choose, and the clock was ticking.
